title: SQL
label: SQL
desc: The standard query language for relational databases: filtering, joins, aggregation, windows and DDL.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install a client and connect to PostgreSQL, MySQL or a SQLite file.

snippets.code:
# Clients on Debian or Ubuntu; sqlite3 is a single binary
sudo apt install -y postgresql-client mysql-client sqlite3

# Connect over TCP, password prompt kept interactive
psql "host=127.0.0.1 port=5432 dbname=inventory user=app_user"
mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -u app_user -p inventory

# SQLite has no server: the file is the database
sqlite3 inventory.db

# PostgreSQL 17 in a container, data on a named volume
docker run --name pg17 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=devsecret -e POSTGRES_DB=inventory \
  -p 5432:5432 -v pg17-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data -d postgres:17

# MySQL 8.4 needs a root password and creates the database on first boot
docker run --name mysql84 -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=devsecret -e MYSQL_DATABASE=inventory \
  -p 3306:3306 -d mysql:8.4

# MariaDB is the fork most distributions ship instead of MySQL
docker run --name mariadb11 -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=devsecret -p 3307:3306 -d mariadb:11

sections.title: Syntax
sections.description: Statements, comments, literal quoting and the rules that trip people up.

snippets.code:
-- One statement is a clause chain that ends with a semicolon
SELECT id, email        -- projection: what comes back
FROM customers          -- source relation
WHERE active = TRUE     -- row filter, before grouping
ORDER BY created_at DESC;  -- final ordering

/* Block comments
   span lines and nest in PostgreSQL */

sections.title: Selecting
sections.description: Project columns, alias them, remove duplicates and page through results.

snippets.code:
-- Computed columns are evaluated per row and never stored
SELECT name,
       price_cents / 100.0 AS price,
       ROUND(price_cents * 0.9 / 100.0, 2) AS sale_price,
       COALESCE(discount_pct, 0) AS discount
FROM products;

sections.title: Filtering and Sorting
sections.description: Narrow rows with predicates, then order the result deterministically.

snippets.code:
-- Comparison, range, set membership and pattern in one predicate list
SELECT id, name, price_cents
FROM products
WHERE price_cents BETWEEN 1000 AND 5000
  AND category IN ('books', 'music')
  AND name LIKE 'The %'
  AND discontinued_at IS NULL;

-- DESC puts the newest first; NULLS LAST keeps missing dates at the end
SELECT id, shipped_at FROM orders
WHERE status = 'shipped'
ORDER BY shipped_at DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC;

-- MySQL has no NULLS LAST: sort on the null flag first
SELECT id, shipped_at FROM orders
WHERE status = 'shipped'
ORDER BY shipped_at IS NULL, shipped_at DESC, id DESC;

-- CASE builds a label; it stops at the first matching branch
SELECT id, total_cents,
       CASE
         WHEN total_cents >= 10000 THEN 'large'
         WHEN total_cents >= 2500 THEN 'medium'
         ELSE 'small'
       END AS bucket
FROM orders
WHERE NOT (status = 'cancelled' OR status = 'refunded');

sections.title: Joins
sections.description: Combine relations by key, keeping unmatched rows when the question needs them.

snippets.code:
-- INNER JOIN keeps only rows that match on both sides
SELECT o.id, o.total_cents, c.email
FROM orders AS o
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = o.customer_id;

-- LEFT JOIN keeps every order, matched or not
SELECT o.id, s.carrier, s.tracking_code
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN shipments AS s ON s.order_id = o.id;

-- Anti-join: orders that have no shipment row yet
SELECT o.id
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN shipments AS s ON s.order_id = o.id
WHERE s.order_id IS NULL;

-- The same question with NOT EXISTS, usually the better plan
SELECT o.id FROM orders AS o
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM shipments AS s WHERE s.order_id = o.id);

-- Self join: employee to manager, LEFT so the top of the tree survives
SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager
FROM employees AS e
LEFT JOIN employees AS m ON m.id = e.manager_id;

-- FULL OUTER JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both sides, MySQL lacks it
SELECT c.id AS customer_id, o.id AS order_id
FROM customers AS c
FULL OUTER JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.id IS NULL OR o.id IS NULL;

sections.title: Aggregation
sections.description: Collapse rows into groups and filter the groups afterwards.

snippets.code:
SELECT customer_id,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       SUM(total_cents) AS revenue_cents,
       ROUND(AVG(total_cents), 2) AS average_ticket,
       MIN(created_at) AS first_order,
       MAX(created_at) AS last_order
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id;

-- WHERE filters rows before grouping, HAVING filters groups after it
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE created_at >= DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY orders DESC;

-- COUNT(*) counts rows, COUNT(column) skips NULLs
SELECT COUNT(*) AS all_rows,
       COUNT(shipped_at) AS shipped_rows,
       COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers
FROM orders;

-- PostgreSQL and SQLite: string_agg; MySQL and MariaDB: GROUP_CONCAT
SELECT customer_id, string_agg(status, ', ' ORDER BY created_at) AS statuses
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id;

sections.title: Subqueries
sections.description: Use a query as a value, a set or a derived table.

snippets.code:
-- Scalar subquery in the select list: one value, repeated per row
SELECT id, total_cents,
       (SELECT AVG(total_cents) FROM orders) AS overall_average
FROM orders;

-- Subquery in a predicate: customers that ordered this year
SELECT id, email FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE created_at >= DATE '2026-01-01');

-- Correlated: the inner query runs per outer row and reads o.total_cents
SELECT o.id, o.total_cents
FROM orders AS o
WHERE o.total_cents > (
  SELECT AVG(i.total_cents)
  FROM orders AS i
  WHERE i.customer_id = o.customer_id
);

-- Derived table: an unnamed subquery in FROM, it must carry an alias
SELECT bucket.customer_id, bucket.revenue_cents
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) AS revenue_cents
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS bucket
WHERE bucket.revenue_cents > 50000;

sections.title: Common Table Expressions
sections.description: Name intermediate results, including recursive walks of a tree.

snippets.code:
-- A CTE is a named subquery scoped to one statement
WITH recent AS (
  SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents
  FROM orders
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) AS revenue_cents
FROM recent
GROUP BY customer_id;

-- Several CTEs chain in order and can reference the earlier ones
WITH paid AS (
  SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
),
totals AS (
  SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) AS revenue_cents FROM paid GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.email, t.revenue_cents
FROM totals AS t
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = t.customer_id
ORDER BY t.revenue_cents DESC;

-- Recursive CTE: walk the category tree from the roots down
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT id, name, parent_id, 0 AS depth
  FROM categories
  WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.id, c.name, c.parent_id, t.depth + 1
  FROM categories AS c
  JOIN tree AS t ON c.parent_id = t.id
)
SELECT id, name, depth FROM tree ORDER BY depth, name;

sections.title: Window Functions
sections.description: Compute per-row values over a partition without collapsing the rows.

snippets.code:
-- ROW_NUMBER is unique per row, RANK repeats on ties and then skips
SELECT id, customer_id, total_cents,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY total_cents DESC) AS position,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY total_cents DESC) AS ranking
FROM orders;

-- Running total and the previous row, all in one pass over the partition
SELECT id, created_at, total_cents,
       SUM(total_cents) OVER (ORDER BY created_at, id) AS running_total,
       LAG(total_cents) OVER (ORDER BY created_at, id) AS previous_total,
       total_cents - LAG(total_cents) OVER (ORDER BY created_at, id) AS delta
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id = 42;

-- Windows cannot go in WHERE: rank in a subquery, filter outside it
SELECT customer_id, id, total_cents
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id, id, total_cents,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY total_cents DESC) AS position
  FROM orders
) AS ranked
WHERE position <= 2;

sections.title: Insert
sections.description: Add rows, copy query results and resolve conflicts without a second round trip.

snippets.code:
-- PostgreSQL and SQLite: ON CONFLICT needs a unique index on email
INSERT INTO customers (email, name)
VALUES ('ana@example.com', 'Ana Ribeiro')
ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name;

-- MySQL 8.0.19 and later use a row alias for the incoming values
INSERT INTO customers (email, name)
VALUES ('ana@example.com', 'Ana Ribeiro') AS incoming
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE name = incoming.name;

sections.title: Update and Delete
sections.description: Change and remove rows, with the predicate you tested as a SELECT first.

snippets.code:
UPDATE products
SET price_cents = price_cents + 500,
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE category = 'books';

-- PostgreSQL: UPDATE ... FROM takes the filter from another table
UPDATE orders AS o
SET status = 'cancelled'
FROM customers AS c
WHERE c.id = o.customer_id AND c.email = 'ana@example.com' AND o.status = 'pending';

-- MySQL and MariaDB: UPDATE with a JOIN
UPDATE orders AS o
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = o.customer_id
SET o.status = 'cancelled'
WHERE c.email = 'ana@example.com' AND o.status = 'pending';

sections.title: DDL
sections.description: Create and reshape tables; most engines commit each of these implicitly.

snippets.code:
CREATE TABLE customers (
  id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  country     CHAR(2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'BR',
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

sections.title: Constraints
sections.description: Let the database reject bad rows instead of trusting every caller.

snippets.code:
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
               CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled')),
  total_cents  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (total_cents >= 0),
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- PostgreSQL: the foreign key is checked at COMMIT, not per statement
ALTER TABLE order_items
  ADD CONSTRAINT order_items_order_fk
  FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES orders (id)
  ON DELETE CASCADE
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED;

sections.title: Indexes
sections.description: Make reads cheap and writes slightly slower; measure before adding one.

sections.title: Transactions
sections.description: Group statements so they all land or none do.

sections.title: NULLs
sections.description: Missing values propagate through arithmetic and never compare equal.

snippets.code:
-- COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument
SELECT id,
       COALESCE(shipped_at, created_at) AS effective_date,
       COALESCE(discount_pct, 0) AS discount,
       NULLIF(quantity, 0) AS quantity_or_null
FROM order_items;
